claims.claim_ar: حرف الجر «إِلَى» (في صورة «إِلَيْهِ») قد يتعلّق بفعلٍ محذوفٍ؛ وبالتالي «إِلَيْهِ» في الموضع قد يكون متعلّقًا بفعلٍ محذوفٍ في السياق النحوي.
claims.claim_en: The preposition 'ilā' (in the form 'ilayhi') can be attached to an omitted (elliptical) verb; thus the 'ilayhi' here may be governed by an elided verb in the syntactic context.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted passage in al-Tibyan discusses a general case of «إلى» attaching to an omitted verb in a different verse/example; applying it to this specific occurrence (إِلَيْهِ) is an extrapolation and should be checked against commentators who treat this verse directly.

claims.claim_ar: حرف الجر «إِلَى» قد يتعلّق بفعلٍ محذوفٍ بحسب التبيان؛ فـ«إِلَى قُوَّتِكُمْ» يمكن قراءته على أنه متعلق بفعلٍ محذوفٍ في التركيب النحوي للآية.
claims.claim_en: The preposition 'ilā' can be related to an omitted verb according to al-Tibyan; therefore 'ilā quwwatikum' (to your strength) may be read as attached to an elided verb in the verse's syntactic structure.
